subject: MSA + Order Form: scope attachments, signing party, and residency clarifications
messages:
From: Priya Shah <pshah@stellalabs.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Green <marcus.green@stellalabs.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: draft and a couple of quick questions

Hi Neha,

Attaching the draft order form and the Exhibit A SOW for your intake team. We're hoping to close procurement by the end of June, so trying to get an initial redline pass this week if possible. A few quick questions to help your legal team triage: 

- Which MSA template will you be using for new customers — the standard Redwood MSA or the enterprise template with data residency rider?
- We need to confirm whether hosting residency can be restricted to US-only for our account. Is that something Redwood Dedicated or Private supports for managed deployments?
- Our signatory for commercial commitments is Marcus Green (VP Finance). Should we list Stella Labs, Inc. as the counterparty or the holding company (Stella Labs Holdings)?

Attachments: Stella_OrderForm_Draft.pdf, Stella_ExhibitA_SOW.docx

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation on the above and any intake checklist you'd like us to fill.

Best,
Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Procurement | Stella Labs
pshah@stellalabs.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <pshah@stellalabs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: draft and a couple of quick questions

Hi Priya — thanks for sending these over and for the timeline context. Looping in Marissa (onboarding) and Kimberly (legal) so we can triage quickly. High-level answers while the team reviews the attachments: 

- Template: we normally start with the standard Redwood MSA; for customers requiring residency or specific enterprise controls we route to the enterprise template + residency rider. Please indicate residency requirement on the intake sheet.
- Residency: US-only residency is supported on Redwood Dedicated and Private; we'll confirm the deployment mode in the intake. If you need contractual residency language in the MSA, Kimberly will scope that.
- Counterparty: confirm which legal entity is taking the obligation. Marcus being signer for commercial obligations is fine — please provide a completed party sheet with full legal name, address, and EIN.

I've attached our intake workbook (redline-intake-sheet.xlsx) — can you fill the party sheet tab and the hosting preference (Dedicated vs Private) and return? Once we have that, Kimberly will prioritize a first-pass redline. Proposed cadence: intake returned by EOD Wed 5/19, legal first-pass by Fri 5/21. If procurement needs to accelerate, flag here.

Next steps: 
1) Complete the intake workbook (party + hosting tab)
2) Confirm signatory name and authority (Marcus)
3) Let us know if SOC2 attestation copy or any security evidence should be attached now

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Marcus Green <marcus.green@stellalabs.com>

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: draft and a couple of quick questions

Thanks Neha — quick replies inline below and attached the filled party info for speed.

> Which MSA template...
We'll accept the enterprise template if the residency rider is required. For cost reasons we'd prefer Dedicated in us-west-2 but can consider Private if residency language is mandatory.

> Residency: US-only supported?
Yes, we need US-only residency. Dedicated is preferred (lower cost).

> Counterparty: which legal entity?
Use: Stella Labs, Inc.
EIN: 12-3456789
Address: 890 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94103

Attaching: Stella_Party_Sheet_filled.pdf and the draft OrderForm (signed placeholder). Marcus notes we need to keep the renewal terms and seat-count billing flexible; procurement will push if we can't get a clear renewal cap.

Appreciate the fast turnaround Marcus — got the party sheet. 

Quick intake note from Onboarding: can you confirm the expected seat count and planned go-live month in the same sheet (we need this for capacity planning and billing exhibit mapping). If you have preferred billing contact (email), add that too.

- Rishi: please review pricing block in the order form for any deviations from standard pricing tables and flag for commercial review.

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <pshah@stellalabs.com>, Marcus Green <marcus.green@stellalabs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: draft and a couple of quick questions

Hi Priya/Marcus — thanks for the party sheet and residency note. We will proceed with the enterprise MSA + residency rider as requested. Initial legal priorities (first-pass): 

1) Residency language: insert a residency rider in Section 2.3 clarifying data and compute residency in US-only and enumeration of the Dedicated pool.
2) Renewal & seat billing: limit auto-renewal notice window to 60 days (customer request) and convert monthly seat billing references to per-seat monthly billing with an annual cap — we will propose language that preserves flexibility but clarifies invoicing cadence.
3) Liability & indemnity: remove the one-way indemnity carveout for third-party claims related to customer data; propose standard mutual indemnity with carveouts for open-source.

I've attached a short redline checklist and will produce a tracked redline of the MSA and Order Form after we get the final intake workbook with the seat count and billing contact. If procurement needs an earlier markup, we can do a partial tracked pass on key clauses (residency, renewal, liability) by EOD Thu 5/20.

Attachments: redline-intake-sheet.xlsx (filled), initial-legal-priorities.txt

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
